value_proposition: Full-stack neutral-atom quantum computing combining Sqale hardware, logical-qubit/error-detection capabilities, individually addressed operations, all-to-all connectivity, and the Superstaq optimizing software stack. Infleqtion positions this architecture as a path toward scalable, commercially useful fault-tolerant computing, while also offering applications research and on-premise access.
qubit_modality: Optically trapped neutral-atom qubits, with dual-species atom arrays referenced as part of the error-correction platform and Rydberg excitation used for entangling operations.
computing_models: Quantum simulation, optimization, and machine-learning workloads
hardware_architecture: Sqale uses neutral atoms in large optical arrays, with individual optical addressing, individually addressed entangling gates, parallel gate addressing, 2D acousto-optic-deflector beam steering, non-destructive readout, and all-to-all connectivity. The company describes dual-species arrays and low-crosstalk measurements as foundations for error correction. Future systems are intended to incorporate photonic-integrated circuits for laser generation, frequency control, and atom addressing.
current_systems: 2025 Sqale system: available on-premise, private-beta cloud access, 100+ physical qubits, 8+ logical qubits with error detection, all-to-all connectivity, and mid-circuit measurement and feedback
Sqale installation at the UK National Quantum Computing Centre
Company-stated Sqale installations in national laboratories worldwide
Demonstrated UK neutral-atom array of 16×16 sites in February 2025
physical_qubit_scale: The current 2025 Sqale specification states 100+ physical qubits. Infleqtion separately reports demonstrated neutral-atom arrays of up to 1,600 sites; the supplied material does not establish that all 1,600 sites constitute an operational 1,600-qubit computer.
demonstrated_logical_qubits: The current 2025 Sqale specification states 8+ logical qubits with error detection. Infleqtion also reports logically encoded materials-science computation and logical-qubit decryption demonstrations, but the supplied material does not state the logical-qubit counts for those demonstrations.
one_qubit_fidelity: Current representative figures are 99.9% for local Rz operations and 99.98% for global R(theta,phi) operations. The source does not provide a single generalized one-qubit gate-fidelity metric.
two_qubit_fidelity: For the current 2025 Sqale specification, representative CZ fidelity is 99.48% with post-selection and 98.8% raw. Separately, Infleqtion reports a published user-facing CZ fidelity of 99.73% ± 0.03% from August 2024. The supplied material does not reconcile the different test conditions or metrics.
connectivity: All-to-all connectivity is stated for the current 2025 Sqale system and for the upcoming configuration.
gate_speed: No numerical one- or two-qubit gate time is disclosed. The company claims a high shot rate and describes future QEC cycle time as order-of-milliseconds; the current QEC cycle time is listed as N/A.
error_correction_strategy: Currently demonstrated capabilities center on logical encoding with quantum error detection, post-selection, mid-circuit measurement and feedback, and non-destructive readout. A December 2024 materials-science demonstration applied quantum error detection to logically encoded qubits. Infleqtion also reports a JP Morgan collaboration on an open-source QEC library intended to reduce physical-qubit requirements by 10–100×. The supplied sources do not demonstrate full active error correction at scale.
fault_tolerance_strategy: Infleqtion plans to progress from error-detected logical qubits to utility-scale fault-tolerant systems using dual-species neutral-atom arrays, low-crosstalk measurement, logical operations, motion plus in-place entanglement, mid-circuit feedback, and scalable photonic control. Despite marketing Sqale as a line of fault-tolerant computers, the current specification lists error detection and no current QEC cycle time, so fault-tolerant operation is not established as currently achieved by the supplied evidence.
roadmap: Upcoming Sqale configuration: 500+ physical qubits, 99.6% representative CZ fidelity, 99.9%+ local Rz fidelity, 99.98%+ global rotation fidelity, all-to-all connectivity, and order-of-milliseconds QEC cycle time; these are upcoming targets, not demonstrated current specifications.

The roadmap table lists upcoming logical-qubit targets of 50+ with error detection and also 10+ with error detection, but the supplied formatting does not clarify whether these correspond to separate configurations or milestones.
Cloud availability for the upcoming system is described as expected; current access is only a private beta.
The homepage targets more than 100 logical qubits by 2028; this is a future target, not an achieved capability.
Future QPUs are intended to scale to many thousands of qubits using photonic-integrated circuits, PIC-based laser arrays, miniature frequency combs, and MEMS spatial light modulators.
Future photonic integration is projected to reduce size, weight, and power by up to 10,000× and support desktop-class systems; these are projections rather than demonstrated system-level results.

strengths: Current evidence of logical encoding and error detection, including an application-oriented materials-science demonstration rather than only component benchmarking
Current 8+ logical-qubit specification with error detection and 100+ physical-qubit on-premise system
All-to-all connectivity can reduce routing and SWAP overhead relative to connectivity-constrained architectures
Strong disclosed entangling-gate results, including 99.73% ± 0.03% user-facing CZ fidelity in a published 2024 result
Individual optical addressing, parallel addressing, mid-circuit measurement, feedback, and non-destructive readout provide relevant building blocks for error-corrected computation
Full-stack capability through Superstaq, with hardware-aware pulse-level optimization and support for major open development frameworks
Existing on-premise installation at the NQCC and private-beta cloud access demonstrate more than a laboratory-only model
Cross-industry and government partnerships provide application-development channels and potential early customers
Integrated-photonics work directly addresses the laser-system size, cost, and portability challenges identified by the company
weaknesses: Current evidence supports error detection, not demonstrated scalable active error correction or full fault tolerance
The current QEC cycle time is listed as N/A, leaving a central fault-tolerance performance metric unproven

Current raw representative CZ fidelity of 98.8% is materially lower than the post-selected 99.48% figure and the separately reported 99.73% result, making system-level performance difficult to compare without methodology details
The demonstrated 1,600-site array is not shown to be a fully operational 1,600-qubit processor
Cloud availability remains private beta rather than broad public access
No coherence times, numerical gate speeds, logical error rates, circuit depths, throughput figures, or application-scale reliability metrics are disclosed
The roadmap table is ambiguous about the upcoming logical-qubit figures of 50+ and 10+
Broad company deployment and revenue claims combine computing, sensing, and timing, obscuring quantum-computing-specific commercial traction
competitive_differentiators: Neutral-atom architecture combining large arrays, all-to-all connectivity, and individual optical addressing
Published 99.73% ± 0.03% user-facing CZ fidelity claimed as the highest neutral-atom entangling-gate fidelity
Application-level use of logically encoded qubits and error detection in materials science
Reported logical architecture combining atom motion and in-place entanglement
Cross-layer Superstaq optimization spanning algorithms, compilation, pulses, hardware connectivity, and noise
Multi-backend software strategy that supports Infleqtion hardware and competing hardware modalities
Integrated computing, sensing, timing, photonics, and software portfolio, potentially providing diversified customer relationships and funding pathways
technical_risks: Scaling from 100+ physical qubits and error-detected logical qubits to useful fault-tolerant computation requires active QEC cycles, low logical error rates, and sustained circuit depth that are not demonstrated in the supplied material
The gap between raw and post-selected CZ fidelity indicates that reported performance may depend substantially on discarding unsuccessful runs
Large site counts do not by themselves establish uniform loading, control, fidelity, usable qubit yield, or application-scale computation across the full array
Dual-species operation, atom motion, in-place entanglement, measurement, and feedback introduce integration and calibration complexity as system size grows
The order-of-milliseconds QEC cycle time is only an upcoming target and could constrain logical clock speed or correction effectiveness
Photonic integration must replace large optical-table components without degrading laser stability, frequency control, addressing precision, or fidelity
No disclosed coherence, gate-time, logical-error-rate, or end-to-end throughput data makes fault-tolerance and application-performance projections difficult to validate
The claim that an open-source QEC library can reduce physical-qubit requirements by 10–100× is not accompanied here by system-level demonstrations on Sqale
commercialization_risks: Private-beta cloud access limits broad developer experimentation and ecosystem growth relative to generally available services
On-premise neutral-atom systems may face substantial installation, maintenance, calibration, and customer-support requirements
Commercial value depends on progressing beyond error detection to reliable logical computation; the current sources do not establish quantum advantage on customer workloads
The path to 100+ logical qubits by 2028 is aggressive relative to the currently disclosed 8+ error-detected logical qubits
Broad revenue, pipeline, customer, and deployment claims cover Infleqtion's full portfolio and do not establish the commercial scale of Sqale specifically
The upcoming-system specifications are pre-order or expected capabilities rather than delivered performance
The company targets many industries, but most supplied application claims describe future opportunity, research, workshops, or co-development rather than production quantum-computing value
marketing_message: Infleqtion presents neutral atoms as naturally scalable qubits and Sqale as a full-stack path from today's error-detected logical computation to commercially viable fault-tolerant quantum advantage. Its message emphasizes high-fidelity entangling gates, all-to-all connectivity, individual addressing, integrated software, and future photonic miniaturization for real-world systems.
messaging_gaps: The phrase 'fault-tolerant neutral atom quantum computers' is stronger than the disclosed current evidence, which shows error detection and lists current QEC cycle time as N/A
The claim that neutral atoms are scalable to millions of qubits is not supported by a demonstrated million-qubit system in the supplied sources
The 1,600-site demonstration is presented near system capabilities without clarifying usable qubit count, loading yield, or full-array computational performance
The relationship between the published 99.73% CZ result, current 99.48% post-selected fidelity, and current 98.8% raw fidelity is not explained
The roadmap table's two upcoming logical-qubit figures are not clearly labeled
Claims of systems in national labs worldwide do not identify installations, configurations, delivery dates, or operational usage beyond the NQCC example
Company-wide claims of hundreds of customers and more than three dozen deployed programs are not segmented by quantum computing, sensing, timing, or software
Application claims often describe potential impact without quantified customer outcomes or demonstrated quantum advantage
